newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse bull run stretches valuations.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse bull run stretches valuations.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, after a slow start, resumed its months-old bull on Tuesday, closing at a new record high, stretching valuations further.

With the exception of Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL), cooling off after weeks of bank merger speculation, and steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, correcting of steep rise in the past weeks, virtually all blue chip shares posted impressive gains.
Cyclicals and dollar-sensitives led the dance, with non- ferrous metals group Union Miniere up five pct at 3,535 and chemical group Tessenderlo up 4.5 pct at 1,850.
The Bel-20 index closed 27.90 points or 1.17 percent higher at 2408.60.
"All the leading shares in the market are now relatively high-priced, but as long as interest rates remain this low, I do not expect valuations to come down," one trader said.

Shipper CMB, up nearly five percent at midsession, ended 2.7 percent higher at 2,485 francs, despite continued speculation the share may be thrown out of the Bel-20 index at the year-end index revision. CMB had underperformed the index since April.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
